verdict.rationale: Vercel documents a 'Redis on Vercel' path: you provision an external Redis (e.g. Upstash) through its Marketplace, and credentials are injected into the project for caching and real-time data. However, its own Vercel KV store is discontinued, so the key-value store is third-party rather than native. missing for 10: a first-party Redis-compatible store, any documentation of job-queue use, latency specifics, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can use a Redis-compatible key-value store for low-latency caching and job queues

citations.quote: Vercel lets you connect external Redis databases through the Marketplace, allowing you to integrate high-performance caching and real-time data storage into your Vercel projects without managing Redis servers.
Vercel KV is no longer available. If you had an existing Vercel KV store, we automatically moved it to Upstash Redis in December 2024.
